Title: Diagnosis
Details: The test failure involves `testIterateDOM` in `AliasedNamespaceIterationTest` which calls `doTestIterate(DocumentContainer.MODEL_DOM)`. The `doTestIterate` method expects the pointer iteration over XPath "/a:doc/a:elem" to yield two distinct elements "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]" and "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]", even though both use the same namespace URI "ns" but different prefixes "a" and "b".

The current bug report indicates that `JXPathContext.iteratePointers()` incorrectly returns the first element twice when there are multiple prefixes for the same namespace URI (e.g., elements with prefixes "a" and "b" both mapped to "ns"). This causes the second element to be omitted from the iteration result.

Looking at the relevant code: 
- `AliasedNamespaceIterationTest.createContext` creates the context and registers namespace prefix "a" with URI "ns".
- The pointer iterator test (`assertXPathPointerIterator`) relies on `ctx.iteratePointers(xpath)`.
- `JXPathContext.iteratePointers(String xpath)` is abstract here, but should handle namespaces accordingly.

The root cause is that the iteration over XPath in `JXPathContext` does not handle the case where multiple prefixes map to the same namespace URI. It treats the XPath using "a" prefix and cannot distinguish elements in the same namespace but with different prefixes, causing duplicated results for elements with the first prefix and missing elements for other prefixes.

Thus, the bug occurs because the underlying XPath evaluation or pointer iteration logic uses only one prefix-to-namespace mapping (e.g., the first encountered) when matching elements, rather than recognizing all prefixes that map to the same namespace URI.

This explains why the test expecting both "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[1]" and "/a:doc[1]/a:elem[2]" fails: only the first pointer is returned twice.

The fix would require ensuring the namespace handling during pointer iteration comprehensively supports multiple prefixes bound to the same namespace URI.

Next, investigation should continue in the implementation of `JXPathContext.iteratePointers` or classes that implement this method and handle namespace context/prefix resolution during XPath evaluation and iteration. Also, checking how the namespace registration and XPath parsing relate to prefix matching for elements would be key.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
